title: RampPilot: micro-exposure storyboard & reversible traffic scenarios
creator: Ava Mitchell
description: Design a compact storyboard and interaction model for very small, reversible traffic exposures (micro-exposures) targeted at rapid canary checks and low-risk A/B experiments. Focus on making safe rollback obvious, surfacing health signals inline, and reducing cognitive load for non-traffic-engineer operators. Must integrate with existing rollout routes, cost dashboard hooks, and the traffic history timeline.
goals: Offer a 3-step micro-exposure flow that can be completed in under 2 minutes for experienced users
Explicitly surface rollback options (auto, manual, emergency) with clear expected outcomes
Show cost delta estimate before ramping (tokens/sec and monthly delta)
Expose signal thresholds and allow quick editing of stop/rollback criteria
Provide a timeline snapshot to compare baseline vs exposure side-by-side
success_metrics: Reduce median time-to-first-traffic for small experiments from 8min -> <3min
Decrease percentage of rollbacks requiring manual investigation by 30%
User test SUS score >= 80 for canary creation flow
<5% of micro-exposure starts without configured stop conditions
decisions: Primary CTA: Start micro-exposure (inline confirmation modal with cost + signals summary)
Default exposure duration: 10 minutes, with quick presets (1m, 5m, 10m, custom)
Stop conditions are required before enabling Start (signal thresholds OR manual stop)
Rollback UI will present three tiers: Auto-revert, Soft-snapback (gradual), Emergency-evac (immediate)
Traffic split granularity: allow 0.1% increments down to 0.1% for micro-audiences
review_feedback: PM (Lina Ortega): Add explicit cost-explain CTA linking to per-route cost breakdown in console
Eng (Marcus Lee): Need data contract for telemetry events: start/expose/stop/rollback with sample IDs
SRE (Priya Nair): Emergency-evac must bypass batching heuristics; require a separate API flag
Design lead (Tom Ruiz): Consider an inline simulation preview to show expected user distribution
Accessibility (Janelle Park): Ensure color-contrast on traffic heat markers and keyboard flow for modal
usability_findings: Users appreciated the single-line summary of stop conditions; 4/7 testers misinterpreted 'soft-snapback' label initially
Participants wanted a visual before/after token cost estimate, not raw numbers only
Two testers tried to pause instead of stop; need clearer distinction and tooltip copy
Non-technical PMs asked for a suggested set of signals based on common regressions (latency, error-rate, hallucination score)
prototype_notes: Added 'snapshot compare' card that renders a side-by-side ephemeral timeline and sample responses for baseline vs exposure
Inline health badges (green/yellow/red) tied to live telemetry and synthetic probes
Confirmation modal now includes estimated token cost delta and a small 'confidence' bar for signal sensitivity
Keyboard-first flow implemented for Start and Emergency-evac actions
risks_and_tradeoffs: Showing estimated cost may deter experiments; mitigated by providing both absolute and delta views
Defaulting to short durations reduces exposure risk but may miss slow regressions; recommend recommended presets
Emergency-evac bypasses some optimizations which can increase immediate cost; must be rate-limited
next_steps: Incorporate Eng telemetry contract (owner: Marcus) and update prototype events
Run 6 moderated usability sessions w/ product managers and platform engineers (owner: Ava)
Add per-route cost link and unit-economics tooltip per PM feedback
Engineering spike to add emergency-evac API flag and telemetry fields (owner: Ravi)
Finalize copy for rollback tiers and run accessibility review
